description: Student replication of post-earnings-announcement drift (Bernard-Thomas) conditioned on Google Trends investor attention (Da-Engelberg-Gao) and same-day earnings congestion (Hirshleifer-Lim-Teoh), for 16 US mega-caps (no ABNB). Grain: one row per earnings event (t=0 announcement, CAR[0,1] surprise, CAR[2,21] drift, count of same-day announcers, high-distraction flag) plus a weekly ticker-level attention panel built from 4 hand-downloaded Google Trends terms per ticker and a daily return matrix from yfinance. Source: yfinance earnings dates/prices and manual Google Trends CSV downloads (a download plan and naming convention are committed, but no pull dates). For ABNB, the value is the scaffold - the event-study code and the drift-by-attention/distraction base rates (drift +0.7% low-distraction vs -1.1% high-distraction, n=238) can be re-run on ABNB's 5 Nov print and its 2020-2026 event history; the Trends pull plan is a template, not point-in-time provenance.
issues: No LICENSE file - reuse rights undetermined (tos_or_license_flag). Google Trends CSVs were downloaded manually via the browser UI; the instructions give settings (US, past 5y, web search) but NOT the pull date, so the attention panel is a single vintage, not point-in-time (gap #4 only partly served). Data covers 16 mega-caps, no ABNB or travel names; earnings dates come from yfinance and are not independently verified. Small n (238 merged events) makes the drift base rates indicative only. The 483 KB PDF write-up and Output/cache/ were skipped per the sample plan; the Trends notebook was not re-run.
